findings.detail: The FARA history reveals three phases: (1) Cold War era (1963-66): Government representation for Israel and Morocco — both sensitive geopolitical clients. (2) Trade defense era (1982-1990): Heavy Korean industrial representation (4 principals), Japanese electronics (NEC), British mining (Consolidated Gold Fields during Minorco hostile takeover), Polish government (post-Communist transition). The Government of Israel representation in 1965 is the earliest FARA registration and places the firm in Israel advocacy during the pre-Six Day War period. All registrations are terminated by 2002, suggesting the firm moved to unregistered foreign work or stopped foreign principal work entirely. Notable: the Korean representation is the deepest — 6 separate Korean principals across 16 years.

curation.lead:
Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP is an elite New York law firm that served as the primary outside counsel for both Apollo Global Management and its co-founder Leon Black’s personal affairs, generating an estimated $100 million or more in annual fees from the Apollo relationship alone. DOJ Volume 11 email records reveal that Brad Karp, the firm’s chairman from 2008 to February 2026, maintained a personal social and professional relationship with Jeffrey Epstein spanning at least 2013 through March 2019, four months before Epstein’s arrest. At least six Paul Weiss partners—Karp, Alan Halperin, Brad Finkelstein, Richard Bronstein, Brad Okun, and Colin Kelly—corresponded directly with Epstein on Black family tax, estate, and corporate matters, treating Epstein as a de facto member of Black’s legal advisory team rather than as an outside consultant (EFTA02472804, EFTA02667959, EFTA02707648).

The firm’s entanglement with Epstein extended beyond advisory work. Paul Weiss drafted the formal service agreement governing payments from Black to Epstein (EFTA01909135) and prepared Black’s 2013 Will and Revocable Trust documents, which were routed to Epstein for review before Black himself saw them (EFTA02707648). Karp personally visited Epstein at 9 East 71st Street, co-managed intelligence operations with Nardello & Co. including covert recordings on Epstein’s behalf, and in March 2019 responded to Epstein’s request for a “tough civil attny” by saying “I’ve got some ideas” (EFTA02631714). In a November 2016 email to both Karp and Black, Epstein addressed the chairman by first name and demanded an accounting of professional fees across Paul Weiss, Akin Gump, Deloitte, and PwC—functioning as a de facto chief financial officer for Black’s professional service relationships (EFTA02667959).

Paul Weiss simultaneously represented institutions on both sides of Epstein-related litigation. The firm defended JPMorgan Chase against derivative claims arising from the bank’s Epstein relationship, represented Deutsche Bank in LIBOR and regulatory proceedings, and advised Apollo—all while its chairman maintained an undisclosed personal relationship with Epstein. Former Paul Weiss partner Lewis Kaplan, appointed to the SDNY bench in 1994, presided over both the Giuffre v. Maxwell trial and the USVI v. JPMorgan settlement without recusal. When DOJ email disclosures made these relationships public in early 2026, Karp resigned the chairmanship on February 4, 2026, replaced by M&A partner Scott Barshay. The firm had already been weakened by a March 2025 Trump executive order targeting it over partner Mark Pomerantz’s prosecution of Trump, resulting in a $40 million pro bono settlement and the departure of multiple prominent partners including former Attorney General Loretta Lynch’s colleague Damian Williams, former DOJ Antitrust head Jonathan Kanter, and litigator Karen Dunn.

sections.title: The Epstein-Black Legal Infrastructure
sections.content:
Paul Weiss did not merely advise Leon Black on transactions that happened to involve Jeffrey Epstein. The firm constructed the legal architecture that formalized their financial relationship. In January 2013, Eileen Alexanderson of Black Family Partners told Epstein that “Leon gave me the go to wire funds to you” and referenced “a service agreement letter that Paul Weiss drafted which I don’t think you have seen,” directing payment to Financial Trust Company at JPMorgan (EFTA01909135). Paul Weiss thus created the contractual framework under which Black ultimately paid Epstein approximately $158 million in advisory fees.

The firm’s estate planning partner Alan Halperin prepared Black’s 2013 Will and Revocable Trust drafts, which were sent to Epstein by Ada Clapp, the chief legal officer of Elysium Management (Black’s family office), along with a detailed summary and “Flow Chart—2013 Proposed Plan” schematic, all prepared by Paul Weiss (EFTA02707648). Clapp asked Epstein which summaries to forward to Black—meaning Epstein had access to Black’s complete estate plan before Black himself reviewed it. By October 2016, Halperin was performing estate computations at Epstein’s direction, writing to Epstein: “I will send you the numbers. The family office provided the starting point. Paul, Weiss then did the analysis and computations” (EFTA02449062).

Tax partner Richard Bronstein corresponded directly with Epstein in privileged exchanges analyzing whether to sell Black’s business interests to an employee or brother-in-law for tax loss, warning that the IRS would reject the structure and they would “face an ugly choice between settling by giving up 40–60% of the loss or going to Tax Court, which will result in an embarrassing article in the Wall Street Journal” (EFTA02478189). Brad Okun handled IRS limitation questions, Brad Finkelstein participated in conference calls coordinated through Lesley Groff and Clapp, and Colin Kelly in Paul Weiss’s London office worked on tax structures for Phaidon, Black’s UK-based art publisher (EFTA01917949). Epstein was formally listed as a co-author of attorney-client privileged memoranda sent to Paul Weiss: a February 2016 memo on aircraft structuring addressed to Bronstein, copying Black, bore the “FROM: Brad Wechsler, Jeffrey Epstein” line (EFTA02472804).

By August 2017, Epstein was criticizing the quality of Paul Weiss’s tax advice, noting that Bronstein had left the firm and his replacement Okun “said he does not do individuals. Only corps returns” (EFTA02639459). When Barry Cohen of the Black family office defended the advisory team—“We think we have examined it extremely carefully. Ada, Paul Weiss, S&C”—Epstein demanded that Black hire “a senior tax advisor” for $1 million or more per year, calling the existing advisory team “childish” (EFTA02398439). The firm’s multiple billing streams were tracked by Epstein’s financial manager Richard D’Agostino, who noted in December 2014 that he was “still sorting through other Paul Weiss invoices (not included in attached) that were not paid directly by our office” (EFTA02711770), indicating both Epstein and Black entities were paying Paul Weiss separately for overlapping work.

sections.title: Institutional Conflicts and the Revolving Door
sections.content:
Paul Weiss occupied a structurally conflicted position across Epstein-related litigation. The firm defended JPMorgan Chase against derivative claims arising from the bank’s relationship with Epstein, securing a dismissal with prejudice. It also defended JPMorgan in the Bear Stearns securities class action—Bear Stearns being Epstein’s original employer. Simultaneously, Paul Weiss represented Deutsche Bank in LIBOR manipulation proceedings, CFTC swap rate investigations, and a tax shelter inquiry that settled for $533 million, conducting an internal investigation that encompassed 200 interviews and 158 million electronic documents. The firm was thus defending two banks with direct Epstein exposure while its chairman maintained an undisclosed relationship with Epstein himself.

Former Paul Weiss partner Lewis Kaplan, who left the firm for the SDNY bench in 1994, presided over both the Giuffre v. Maxwell trial and the USVI v. JPMorgan settlement. While former-partner judicial assignments do not constitute legal conflicts requiring recusal, the structural overlap is notable: a former partner of the firm simultaneously representing JPMorgan against Epstein-related claims was adjudicating the most consequential Epstein civil litigation.

The firm’s revolving door with the federal government is among the most extensive in American law. Former U.S. Attorney General Loretta Lynch joined as a litigation partner in May 2019. Former DHS Secretary Jeh Johnson, former SDNY U.S. Attorney Damian Williams, former DOJ Antitrust Division head Jonathan Kanter, and former Obama White House counsel Roberto Gonzalez all passed through the firm. Kannon Shanmugam, a former Assistant Solicitor General who clerked for Justice Scalia, has argued 39 Supreme Court cases from Paul Weiss. This personnel pipeline creates an unparalleled network of institutional relationships across the federal judiciary, the DOJ, and regulatory agencies—precisely the kind of access that would be valuable to clients facing federal scrutiny.

The Trump administration targeted this network directly. On March 14, 2025, a presidential executive order against Paul Weiss suspended security clearances, restricted federal building access, and directed contract reviews, citing partner Mark Pomerantz’s role in the Manhattan DA’s prosecution of Trump and the firm’s DEI policies. Paul Weiss settled within six days, committing $40 million in pro bono work for Trump administration priorities, abandoning DEI policies, and adopting political neutrality in client selection. Multiple partners departed in protest, including Karen Dunn, Jeannie Rhee, William Isaacson, Jessica Phillips, Kyle Smith, and Damian Williams. The settlement, widely reported as capitulation, was the first of its kind by a major law firm.

sections.title: The Apollo Relationship and Financial Scale
sections.content:
Apollo Global Management is Paul Weiss’s most significant client relationship. The firm has served as Apollo’s primary outside counsel for decades, handling the $43 billion Athene merger and appearing in 48 SEC filings on Apollo’s behalf. Industry sources have estimated the relationship generates $100 million or more in annual fees. This dependency created enormous institutional pressure for the firm to protect both Apollo and its co-founder Leon Black, whose personal affairs were deeply intertwined with the firm’s work.

Paul Weiss also represented Caesars Entertainment, an Apollo-controlled company, in the Danner v. Caesars securities fraud litigation (SDNY, 1:14-cv-07973), defending against bondholder claims arising from the CEOC restructuring—an Apollo transaction. The firm was simultaneously counseling Apollo and defending Apollo’s portfolio company while being accused of conflict of interest in the CEOC bankruptcy proceedings. The firm’s representation of Apollo’s private equity rival clients is also notable: Paul Weiss represents eight of the ten top global private equity firms, including Blackstone, KKR, TPG, Carlyle, and Warburg Pincus, executing over 1,200 transactions valued at more than $2 trillion since 2020.

The financial dimensions of the Paul Weiss–Epstein relationship are partially visible through DOJ emails. On April 15, 2015, Epstein directed his assistant Melanie Spinella to confirm whether “the Paul Weiss bill got paid” in the same message that outlined $10 million to Gratitude America, $20 million to Financial Trust Company, and a net position of $150 million (EFTA02504960). The Paul Weiss bill was significant enough for Epstein to track alongside eight-figure disbursements. Epstein also directed Gates Foundation General Counsel Connie Collingsworth to use Paul Weiss for securities expertise on a charitable structure, telling her: “I suggest you call Brad Karp, and tell him you are calling at my suggestion. Brad is the managing partner” (EFTA02714105). This confirms Epstein was brokering client introductions to Paul Weiss as a form of relationship currency.

sections.title: Foreign Representation and Political Activity
sections.content:
FARA records document five Paul Weiss registrations spanning 1963 to 2002, representing 14 foreign principals across eight countries. The earliest registration, for the Government of Israel in 1965–1966, placed the firm in Israeli advocacy during the period immediately preceding the Six-Day War. The firm also represented the Government of Morocco (1963), the Government of Poland during its post-Communist transition (1990), and the Government of Botswana (1987–1989). The deepest foreign client relationship was with South Korea: six separate Korean principals across 16 years, including Hyundai Heavy Industries, Samsung Ship Building, the Korea Federation of Textile Industries, Korea Iron & Steel Association, the Embassy of the Republic of Korea, and Korea Telecom.

Domestically, Paul Weiss operated as a registered lobbying firm in 1999–2000, reporting clients including IBP ($180,000), SkyBridge Ltd Partnership ($100,000)—the predecessor of Anthony Scaramucci’s firm—the National Music Publishers Association ($60,000), and Intelsat ($40,000). The firm later hired SKDKNICKERBOCKER on behalf of Carlos Ghosn for $490,000 in 2019 and ACG Advocacy on behalf of Qualcomm for over $600,000 between 2019 and 2021 during the Broadcom hostile takeover defense. FEC records reveal the firm is overwhelmingly Democratic-aligned: Brad Karp alone donated over $200,000 to Democratic committees in 2024–2025, and only one of 34 identified Paul Weiss donor-employees made any Republican contributions. This political profile made the March 2025 Trump executive order settlement, which required political neutrality and pro bono work on administration priorities, particularly jarring for the firm’s partnership.

The firm’s pro-Israel advocacy connections extend beyond FARA. Per LittleSis records, Paul Weiss provided $403,000 in legal and research services to the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a hawkish pro-Israel think tank, in 2017 and maintained a business relationship with AIPAC. Karp co-chaired a November 2023 letter campaign to law school deans on campus antisemitism, broadening definitions to include certain criticism of Israel. This advocacy pattern, spanning 60 years from the 1965 FARA registration through the present, places the firm within the institutional orbit of Israel-connected networks relevant to the broader investigation.
